newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand boosts infrastructure for future trade.
newsitem.headline: Thailand boosts infrastructure for future trade.

text.p: Thailand has embarked on an ambitious second phase of its eastern seaboard (ESB) development programme after the first phase from 1980-1994 did much to raise Thai industrial standards.

Government planners said the ESB expansion called for development of industrial estates, roads and railways covering 11 eastern and central provinces stretching to the Cambodian border to the east and linking up with Thailand's backward northeast region.
They also said Thailand needed new air and sea cargo shipment facilities. A key component of the expanded ESB, is a two-year project to turn a former U.S. airbase at Utapao into an air cargo gateway.
Utapao, a base for American B-52 bombers during the Vietnam War, has a 3.5-km (2.2 mile) runway that can handle over 30 big commercial aircraft per hour.
The base, run by the Thai navy, now serves as a back-up for Bangkok's congested airport and is used mainly by commercial chartered flights and two domestic airlines.

Paul Wedel, executive director of the Kenan Institute Asia consultancy, said neighbour Malaysia had an edge over Thailand as its industries had the benefit of faster decision-making by the government.

The Kenan Institute and four other foreign consultants are completing Thailand's master plan for its $120 million Global Transpark Project (GTP), a complex designed to speed up air cargo shipments out of Thailand.
Wedel said the plan would be ready by October and project construction completed by late 1999.

Phisit Pakkasem, former head of Thailand's long-term economic think-tank, told diplomats at the weekend: "To compete globally, the Thai economy must be adjusted structurally and supported by a new generation of infrastructure."
He projected that by 2020, southeast Asian air cargo traffic would exceed 14.6 million tonnes, of which five million tonnes would be through Thailand.

The economist, heading a government committee to develop Utapao, said the terminal's GTP aimed to provide express air cargo service for shipping time-sensitive goods to any foreign markets within 48 hours.
"GTP represents the perfect project for the millennium as a bridge to the next century," he said.
Other parts of the ESB expansion include upgrades of Laem Chabang and Maptaphut deep-sea ports.

Laem Chabang, 110 km (60 miles) south of Bangkok and 15 km (nine miles) from Pattaya resort, will raise its annual container processing capacity five times, to five million TEUs (20-foot equivalent units) by 2001.
Maptaphut, a heavy industry port for petrochemical, steel, and oil refineries, will be able to accommodate vessels of up to 150,000 dead weight tonnes next year, three times its current capacity.
